html:
SMTO-EXE-0038 — The terminal is already busy with another command

GUID: 9b945bbe-641e-453c-91e2-4ba3a030021d
Slug: terminal-command-busy
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO wanted to start a new command in a terminal that is still running an earlier command it is watching. The new command was not started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the terminal and the task's steps to see which command is still running. Only one watched command can run in a terminal at a time.
  2. If that step shows Waiting for terminal input, type the answer in the terminal, or select Let agent handle. A command waiting for an answer won't finish by itself and keeps the terminal busy.
  3. If the earlier command is stuck and you no longer need it, select Stop. Stopping does not undo what it already did. Ending the stuck command frees the terminal for the next one.

What success looks like

  • The earlier command finishes and the next command starts in the terminal.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the new command; it can't start while the terminal is busy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A detached terminal command was requested while the terminal session still had an active agent-captured command.

What this means

  • A detached terminal command was requested while that terminal already held an active captured-command object. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • A detached terminal command was requested while that terminal already held an active captured-command object.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the same terminal's current capture and its completion/cancellation state.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the terminal session's active captured command (gateway_core.terminal_posix.TerminalSession.start_detached_command) and let it complete, answer its prompt, or cancel it through the task's Stop control before admitting another command. Do not loop resubmissions while the capture is active.
  • Inspect the current command and wait for its completion or stop it through existing controls before submitting another.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing capture settles before the intended next terminal command is admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
